content:
The “Midsommar” star took the chance to pitch herself a part in the new Bond film during her acceptance speech at ELLE’s Women in Hollywood event in Beverly Hills on Monday.

Toward the end of her emotional speech, Pugh addressed Bond director Denis Villeneuve directly.

“I sent Denis a message this morning, and I said, ‘Congratulations on finding a new Bond. Nice catch,” Pugh said while being honored onstage. “Any villains with the size of 5’4’’?”

“Anyway, I’m reminding you just in case!” the actor said as the audience laughed and clapped.

Considering Pugh has worked with both Villeneuve and new Bond Robert Pattinson before, she has a greater chance than some.

Brad Pitt has also said he’d be interested in a potential Bond villain part, telling Extra on Monday, “I’d be up for that.”

“I mean, my man Javier [Bardem] did it so well,” the “Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” actor said, referencing Bardem’s turn as a Bond villain in 2012’s “Skyfall” film.

“It’s tall shoes, but I’d take that on, yeah,” Pitt said, before praising the decision to cast Pattinson for the role.

Pattinson released an enthusiastic statement about the dream part on Monday, calling Bond “one of the most legendary characters in cinema.”

“To be entrusted with 007 is the honor of a lifetime,” he shared. “To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement. I couldn’t be more excited about this partnership and the work ahead with this fantastic team.”
